questions.text: The relays that switch the two rooms are the most expensive part, and no 'switch-and-stay' relay that is also safe enough for 230 V is in stock at the assembler. Which do you prefer for the 10 prototypes?
options: Recommended: larger, cheaper relays (Omron, 16 A, strong 230 V insulation). The board grows to 75 x 48 mm, so the device fills the whole wall box behind a blank cover plate instead of a 3-module insert. About 25 USD per unit (meets your target). Relays are hand-soldered; relay delivery can take weeks, maybe months at some distributors.

Compact relays (Panasonic). Keeps the standard 3-module insert (65 x 42 mm board). About 35 USD per unit (about 10 USD over target). Relays are hand-soldered, and before ordering we need a written statement from Panasonic that they are rated for valve heads and have reinforced 230 V insulation.
Stop and look for a third option (for example a relay with a different coil plus a small extra circuit to drive it): about 1 more design round; cost and size unknown until then.
questions.why: Relay price (3.5 vs 8.5 USD each) and relay size decide both the unit cost (target: under 25 USD for 10 units) and whether the device fits a 3-module insert. See conflicts.md C9.
